the complaints of memory function after E.C.T., as well as the results on the memory tests, vary with the severity of depression before E.C.T.
The complaints of memory disturbances were not related to the memory performances as measured by tests, and that the memory performances were not related to any of the variables studied.
patients who have been treated with E.C.T. complain of disturbances of memory to a varying degree.

the following problems: (a) The extent to which complaints of memory disturbances are related to the degree of memory disturbances measured by tests.
the following problem: What factors are of importance for the complaints of impaired memory after E.C.T.?
the following problems: (1) To what extent do complaints of impaired memory after E.C.T., as reported by the patient, correspond to the results of objective tests of memory function?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
memory disturbances after E. C.T. are due to a complex of factors.

the complaints of impaired memory after E.C.T., to a varying degree, reflect true disturbances, but also to a varying degree are influenced by other factors, which have not been sufficiently investigated.
memory disturbances are common after E.C.T., and are caused by the treatment, but are influenced also by the disease itself and other factors, which have not yet been investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the memory function is not impaired after E.C.T.

the complaints of memory impairments after E.C.T., as measured by the patients' subjective experiences, are not determined only by the objective memory performances as measured by means of psychological tests.

complaints of impaired short-term memory are not related to memory performances measured by means of memory tests, and that they are not determined by the degree of improvement after E.C.T., whereas the complaints are determined by the degree to which patients are satisfied with E.C.T.
The main takeaway from our work is that
memory complaints after E.C.T are related to the patients’ perception of the treatment, rather than to objective memory performance.

the complaints of memory disturbance after E.C.T., as well as the results of memory tests, are influenced not only by the treatment itself, but also by the patient’s state before the treatment, and by his general condition during the treatment period.
memory complaints were related to the severity of the depressive symptoms and not the number of ECT treatments.
